title: Evaluating AI for Law: Bridging the Gap with Open-Source Solutions

bias_targets.methodology: The paper conceptually evaluates the risk of cognitive biases (including conjunction bias, probability weighting, overconfidence, framing effects, anticipated regret, reference dependence, and confirmation bias) in LLMs applied to legal contexts by reviewing existing literature, though it does not empirically measure them in its own preliminary experiments.

The authors assess the lack of diversity in AI-generated responses and the tendency of general-purpose LLMs to replicate dominant worldviews (creating 'AI echo chambers'). They propose mitigating this through a domain-specific framework using crowdsourced expert feedback, rather than measuring it via direct empirical testing in this study.
